clue.text: Philosophical approach exhibited by Tokyo gallery

indicators.note: something exhibited by the words is on show inside them, so the letters are found within Tokyo gallery

explanation.surface: A Japanese art gallery puts a school of philosophy on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is an Indian school of philosophy as well as a discipline of physical and mental practice.

clue.text: Minister put down following split

indicators.note: the piece for put down comes following the one for split

parts.note: to chap is to crack or split, as skin does in the cold
lain is the past participle of lie, so laid down or put down

explanation.surface: A clergyman is brought low after a schism in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution, and minister is a general word for clergy.

clue.text: Decaying eaves harbouring first of downy ducks

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so the rearranged eaves hold a letter inside them
decaying eaves are falling apart, so their letters are broken up and rearranged
first of signals taking the opening letter of downy

explanation.surface: Fluffy ducks nest under the rotting eaves of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decaying' turns EAVES into EVAES, and 'harbouring' puts D inside it. 'Ducks' looks like the birds, but it is the verb: dodges.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge or avoid it, so ducks means avoids.

clue.text: Mayor's office won't broadcast lobby

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of won't are scattered into a new order

parts.note: a lobby is an entrance hall

explanation.surface: A mayor refuses to let lobbyists have their say on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges WONT (the apostrophe of won't drops out) into TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A town hall is the building housing the local council and the mayor's office.

clue.text: See 7 Across
Unknown with Q when conspiring?

definitions.meaning: short for anonymous, of an unnamed author
put Q in front and you have the name of the QAnon conspiracy movement

explanation.walkthrough: QAnon is an American online conspiracy movement; adding Q to the answer spells its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is the abbreviation printed for an unknown author; prefixed by Q it names a notorious conspiracy theory.

clue.text: 23's advice to 25: the reader 'Ought to Buy Shares in Nanotech' (Vol. I free)

parts.note: a clue addresses its reader as you

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the share tip plus Vol. I break loose and rearrange

parts.words: Ought to Buy Shares in Nanotech

parts.note: Vol. is the standard abbreviation for volume, as in Volume I of a book

explanation.surface: Marx advises the workers to put their savings into nanotechnology stocks, citing volume one of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is 23 Down and 25 is 25 Across: Karl Marx addressing the workers. 'free' shuffles the share tip plus Vol. I into the slogan's remainder; Vol. I hints at the first volume of Das Kapital.
explanation.definitionFit: The rallying cry ending The Communist Manifesto by Marx and Engels urges the working classes to rise, as there is nothing to lose.

clue.text: See 7
Batter's finale a representative cricket shot

indicators.note: a finale is the end, so the last letter of Batter's is taken

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A batsman ends an innings with a typical cricket stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The ramp is a cricket stroke in which the batter deflects the ball up and over the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Prison's number one turns up after extra time in pit

indicators.note: after puts the reversed number-one piece behind the rest
in places the piece for extra time inside the one for pit

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or pit in a surface
ET is the abbreviation for extra time in football

indicators.note: turns up in an across clue means the letters are flipped round to run the other way

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: A football match runs into extra time while the prison's top inmate shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' gives ION; 'in' makes DETENT, which 'after' places before ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Detention is confinement, the state of being held in custody, so it can stand for a prison.

clue.text: See 7 Across
Dialectical battle to rule the school?

definitions.meaning: in Marxist dialectic, history is the conflict between social ...
a jokey reading: a fight between pupils for control of the ...

explanation.definitionFit: Class struggle is the Marxist term for conflict between social ranks; playfully it is a fight in a schoolroom.

clue.text: Constrain 109?

parts.note: 100 is C in Roman numerals
9 refers to the answer at 9 Across, a cricket shot

explanation.surface: An instruction to limit something to a figure of one hundred and nine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 109 as 100 (Roman C) followed by 9, the answer to 9 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to restrict or hinder, as in cramping someone's style.

clue.text: Encounters back trouble — is one's drug missing?

indicators.note: back means the word for trouble is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written

indicators.note: missing means the drug letter is left out of the words is one's

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone with back pain asks whether their medication has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AIL into LIA; 'missing' takes E from ONES to leave ONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Liaisons are meetings or contacts, often secret romantic encounters.

clue.text: British bean counters eat Swiss cheesy whatsit

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the auditors' letters surround the Swiss one

parts.note: the NAO, National Audit Office, is the UK body of public-spending auditors
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: British accountants dine on a Swiss cheese-topped snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Bean counters is slang for accountants; the NAO, the UK's National Audit Office, checks government spending.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip served topped with melted cheese, so a cheesy snack.

clue.text: Starts to dwindle as we notice first light

indicators.note: the starts of the next words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: We notice the darkness fading away as morning arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is daybreak, when the first light of morning appears.

clue.text: MI6's last vestiges of moral fibre

parts.note: MI6 is popularly called SIS, the Secret Intelligence Service

indicators.note: the last vestiges are the closing letters of moral, here its final two

explanation.surface: Spies at MI6 retain only the faintest traces of moral fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence agency, officially the Secret Intelligence Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: See 12 Across
German froideur cut to pieces

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for German, as on car plates (Deutschland)
froideur is coolness of manner, iciness

explanation.surface: A German's chilly manner shatters someone's feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice is to chop food into small cubes, cutting it into pieces.

clue.text: Slip up in detectives offloading gear

indicators.note: in puts the mistake word inside the detectives word

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective
to slip up is to make a mistake, to err

explanation.surface: Investigators blunder while unloading their equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip up' looks like a reversal in a down clue, but it is one phrase meaning make a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Derricks are cranes, lifting gear used for loading and unloading ships.

clue.text: Harry, for one, takes boat to get something to put on the barbie

definitions.text: something to put on the barbie

parts.note: Prince Harry, second son, is the spare to the heir, the title of his memoir
a RIB is a rigid inflatable boat

explanation.surface: Prince Harry heads off in a boat to fetch something for a barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heir and a spare' is a British saying for a monarch's first two sons; Harry titled his memoir Spare. 'Barbie' is slang for barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a cut of pork ribs, a classic item to grill at a barbecue.

clue.text: Kindles for everyone accepted by woke school

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: woke and rose both mean got up from sleep
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Ebooks for all are embraced by a progressive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woke' looks like politics but is the past tense of wake, meaning ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse feelings is to stir or kindle them, as in kindling enthusiasm.

clue.text: Comic to go on about bit of opportunity to spoil vote

parts.note: to harp on is to keep talking about something tediously

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A comedian rants about a chance to ruin his ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo Marx was the silent, harp-playing member of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: By what means to include a bishop in drag?

indicators.note: to include means to take the following letters within

parts.note: how asks by what means
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A query about how a bishop might come to be dressed in women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' suggests cross-dressing; here it is the old name for a heavy harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is a heavy farm harrow pulled over ploughed land, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Mopped gents in 21d's nipper

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the answer at 21 Down

parts.note: 21 Down's answer is the possessive pronoun in the slogan

indicators.note: mopped suggests swept around, so the letters of gents are pushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A child tidies the men's toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mopped' gives NGSTE, which 'in' sets inside the 21 Down answer. Gents is British for a men's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is British slang for a small child, so it means a young person.

clue.text: See 7 Across
Doctrines in sciences modified slightly at first

indicators.note: at first means the initial letters of the preceding four words

explanation.surface: Scientific theories that get tweaked a little at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a distinctive doctrine or ideology, like socialism or Marxism.

clue.text: See 20 Across
Stealthily abandon farmland, moving east west

indicators.note: moving signals a letter shifted to a new place within the word
west means the letter travels leftwards, earlier in the word

parts.note: to quit is to abandon
a ley is land temporarily under grass

explanation.surface: Someone slips away from a farm by moving from east to west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' and 'west' shift E leftwards, from after L to before T, turning QUITLEY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Quietly means without noise, the way a stealthy person moves.

clue.text: Staff swore vehemently, accepting hollow rank

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the shuffled letters enclose the other piece
swearing vehemently suggests violent agitation, so the letters of swore are churned
a hollow word has its middle emptied, leaving only first and last letters

explanation.surface: An employee cursed angrily at an empty title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehemently' gives WOERS, and 'accepting' puts the hollowed rank inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff are the employees of an organisation, its workforce.
